metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially > 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then apply mean reversion toward 30-day moving average.
- If true outcome shows early downward trend (e.g., 3–5 consecutive drops), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in decline, especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- When sentiment is positive but model forecast is flat or rising slowly, model underestimates downward pressure; add 1–3% downward bias if sentiment >0.5 and price has not yet broken below 30-day MA.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment is noisy or mixed.
- If sentiment is negative and price drops below 40, model often fails to recognize structural support; add 5–10% buffer below 40 to avoid underestimating support levels.
